Perform a variable-cell relaxation (vc-relax) on BiFeO3, followed by a self-consistent field (SCF) total-energy calculation on the relaxed structure using identical computational settings.
The starting structure is the R3c (space group 161) ferroelectric perovskite phase of BiFeO3 with 10 atoms per primitive cell (2 Bi, 2 Fe, 6 O), using approximate hexagonal lattice parameters a ≈ 5.58 Å and c ≈ 13.86 Å (scaled to 2 formula units) and atomic positions consistent with the R3c Wyckoff assignments (Bi and Fe on 15a, O on 15e).
Use LDA pseudopotentials from PseudoDojo SR_v0.4.1: bi.upf, fe.upf, and o.upf from the LDA_standard set.
Set ecutwfc to 50 Ry.
Set ecutrho to 400 Ry.
Use a 6×6×6 Monkhorst-Pack k-point grid with a half shift (0.5, 0.5, 0.5 in fractional reciprocal-lattice coordinates) for both the vc-relax and the final SCF.
Set etot_conv_thr to 1.0e-8 Ry, forc_conv_thr to 1.0e-7 Ry/bohr, and conv_thr (SCF) to 1.0e-8 Ry.
Use Gaussian smearing with degauss = 0.02 Ry.
Set a starting magnetization of 2.0 μB on each Fe atom and 0.0 μB on Bi and O atoms to help break the initial non-magnetic symmetry.
Do not apply Hubbard U corrections.
Do not include spin-orbit coupling.
Allow full cell relaxation in the vc-relax step (all lattice vectors, atomic positions, and cell volume are free to relax).
After the vc-relax converges, extract the final relaxed structure and run a single-point SCF calculation on that structure with the same ecutwfc, ecutrho, k-point grid, smearing, and convergence thresholds.
Return the fully relaxed atomic structure (cell vectors and fractional coordinates) and the final SCF total energy in Ry.
